title: Adequate affinization after arbitrary base change
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], and let $g:T\to Y$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces over $k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $\mathcal X_T=\mathcal X\times_YT$ and let $f:\mathcal X_T\to T$ be the projection. Use the structure sheaves and direct images of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], the relative spectrum of [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence], and the point spaces of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]. Then $\mathcal B=f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_T}$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-algebra. The structural map $\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal B$ defines an affine morphism $h:H=\operatorname{Spec}_T\mathcal B\to T$, and there is a canonical factorization $f=h\circ a$ with $a:\mathcal X_T\to H$ an adequate moduli space. The map $h$ is a universal homeomorphism: for every algebraic-space morphism $T'\to T$, the induced map $|H\times_TT'|\to|T'|$ is a homeomorphism. No flatness, finite-type, Noetherian or diagonal-separation hypothesis on $g$, $T$, or $\mathcal X$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(3), printed p.509; its adequate homeomorphism implies the stated universal-homeomorphism property by Definition 3.3.1; published primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The $2$-fibre product $\mathcal X_T$ is algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. The adequate-moduli hypothesis includes that $\phi$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These properties persist under arbitrary base change by [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism], so $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-algebra-direct-image] to $f$ and its structure algebra: its smooth-test formula restricts on etale tests exactly to the direct image used in the statement. Thus $\mathcal B=f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_T}$ is quasi-coherent. By [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] it defines the affine space $h:H=\operatorname{Spec}_T\mathcal B\to T$. On each affine etale $W\to T$, put $D_W=\Gamma(\mathcal X_W,\mathcal O)$. That correspondence identifies $H_W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D_W$ and identifies its structural ring map with pullback of functions from $W$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(3), relative-Spec construction; Stacks Tags 04T2, 050V, 050F, 077A, 0GQQ, 081V, 081W; primary published PDF read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Choose affine etale charts $Y_i\to Y$. Pull them back to $T$ and choose affine etale charts $W\to T\times_Y Y_i$; their composites form a jointly surjective etale family over $T$. Existence and preservation of these covers are [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Each $W$ has a specified map to the affine scheme $Y_i$. By [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality], $\phi_i:\mathcal X_i\to Y_i$ is adequate. Its affine global criterion and [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion] show that $\phi_i$ is adequately affine. Apply [lem-sfb-adequately-affine-affine-target-base-change] to $\phi_i$ and $W\to Y_i$. It gives adequate affineness of $f_W:\mathcal X_W\to W$ for every such $W$. Its global power-lifting criterion therefore holds for all quasi-coherent algebra surjections on $\mathcal X_W$, by [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion].

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(3), first sentence of proof; Proposition 4.2.1(6), Remark 4.1.3 and Lemma 4.1.8(3); Stacks 03FX, 02X2, 041F; primary published PDF read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For a chart $W$ from step 2, the structural map $\mathcal X_W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: compose the morphism $f_W$ from step 1 with the affine map $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, using [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-composition-affine]. Thus [lem-sfb-stack-affinization-qcqs] supplies the canonical quasi-compact quasi-separated map $c_W:\mathcal X_W\to\operatorname{Spec}D_W=H_W$. Its map on global functions is $\mathrm{id}_{D_W}$. The composites to $W$ coincide with $f_W$: on every scheme object of $\mathcal X_W$ both correspond to the structural pullback of functions from $W$, so the affine-target correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] identifies them. Hence $c_W$ is a factorization over $W$.

source.place: Remark 5.1.2, the canonical affinization morphism; Stacks 075S, 01I1; primary published PDF read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: These maps glue canonically. Indeed refine each overlap $W\times_TW'$ by affine etale schemes $V$. The algebra map $D_W\to D_V$ is restriction of compatible structure sections. Consequently $c_W|_{\mathcal X_V}$ and the composite of $c_V$ with $H_V\to H_W$ give exactly the same map $D_W\to\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ on every scheme object $P\to\mathcal X_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] they agree on that object. The same calculation with $W'$ proves agreement as maps to $H$. On an arbitrary scheme object $P\to\mathcal X_T$, these maps over the etale cover $P\times_T W$ therefore glue uniquely to a map $P\to H$, because an algebraic space is an etale sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The glued maps commute with every arrow of scheme objects, by uniqueness, and so define a morphism $a:\mathcal X_T\to H$. The equalities over $W$ show $ha=f$. The formula on scheme objects makes the factorization independent of the chosen covers.

source.place: Remark 5.1.2, construction of the natural relative-Spec morphism, with the overlap equality written out; Stacks 081V, 081W, 01I1; primary published PDF read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For each $W$, step 2 gives the global power-lifting property on $\mathcal X_W$; step 3 gives that $c_W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and that $D_W\to\Gamma(\mathcal X_W,\mathcal O)$ is the identity. The affine criterion of [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality] therefore shows that $c_W$ is an adequate moduli space. The maps $H_W=H\times_TW\to H$ form a jointly surjective etale cover, and $a\times_HH_W$ identifies with $c_W$, since $a$ is over $T$. By [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism], $a$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Now apply the etale-local equivalence of [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality] to $a$ and the cover $(H_W\to H)$: $a$ is an adequate moduli space. This application first establishes the qcqs hypothesis required by that equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(3), adequacy of the canonical relative affinization; Remark 5.1.2 and Lemma 4.1.8(3); primary published PDF read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text:
Fix one lifted chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\to Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}R$ from step 2. The projection $q:\mathcal X_W\to\mathcal X_i$ is affine, by the final clause of [lem-sfb-stack-affine-algebra-direct-image]. On every smooth scheme chart $P\to\mathcal X_i$, its base change is $P\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}C\to P$. Ordinary affine pushforward of its structure algebra is $\mathcal O_P\otimes_R C$. The chart characterization in the same node thus identifies $q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_W}$ with $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_i}\otimes_R C$. Its global-section isomorphism gives
$$D_W=\Gamma(\mathcal X_W,\mathcal O)\cong\Gamma(\mathcal X_i,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_i}\otimes_R C).$$
Under this identification the map $C\to D_W$ defining $h_W$ sends $c$ to the compatible sections $1\otimes c$, because both are pullback of the regular function $c$ from $W$. This identifies the actual structural map, not merely its source and target rings.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(3), identification of the algebra adjunction unit with the affine-base-change structure map; Stacks 0GQY, 081V; primary published PDF read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-algebra-unit-power-kernel] to the adequate space $\phi_i:\mathcal X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and the $R$-algebra $C$ of step 6. For every commutative $C$-algebra $C'$ the map $C'\to C'\otimes_C D_W$ has nilpotent kernel and a positive power of every target element in its image, so [lem-pur-all-element-powers-spectrum-homeomorphism] makes $|\operatorname{Spec}(C'\otimes_C D_W)|\to|\operatorname{Spec}C'|$ a homeomorphism. By the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] this is the base change of $h_W$ along $\operatorname{Spec}C'\to W$. Hence, componentwise, $|H_W\times_WV|\to|V|$ is a homeomorphism for every scheme $V\to W$ that is a disjoint union of affine schemes. Now let $\mathcal T\to W$ be any algebraic stack and $p:\mathcal T_H=H_W\times_W\mathcal T\to\mathcal T$; all fibre products here are algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal T$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], refined so that $V$ is a disjoint union of affine schemes; its base change $V_H=H_W\times_WV\to\mathcal T_H$ is again a smooth surjective atlas. By [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets], $|p|$ is continuous, $|V|\to|\mathcal T|$ and $|V_H|\to|\mathcal T_H|$ are open surjections inducing the quotient topologies, the fibres of $|V|\to|\mathcal T|$ are the classes given by $|R|$ with $R=V\times_{\mathcal T}V$, and points of $2$-fibre products surject onto fibre products of point sets. Surjectivity: a point $\tau\in|\mathcal T|$ lifts to $v\in|V|$, and the point of $|V_H|$ over $v$ maps to a point over $\tau$. Injectivity: let $z_1,z_2\in|\mathcal T_H|$ lie over $\tau$; lift them to $e_1,e_2\in|V_H|$ lying over $v_1,v_2\in|V|$. Since $v_1,v_2$ lie over $\tau$, some $r\in|R|$ has $s(r)=v_1$, $t(r)=v_2$, and some point of $|H_W\times_WR|$ lies over $r$. Its images under the two projections to $|V_H|$ lie over $v_1$ and $v_2$, hence equal $e_1$ and $e_2$, because the fibres of $|V_H|\to|V|$ are singletons; the two composites $H_W\times_WR\to\mathcal T_H$ are $2$-isomorphic, so $z_1=z_2$. Closedness: for closed $Z\subseteq|\mathcal T_H|$ its inverse image in $|V_H|$ is closed, so its image in $|V|$ is closed; by the bijectivity just shown this image is the inverse image of $|p|(Z)$, which is therefore closed in the quotient topology. Thus $|p|$ is a continuous closed bijection, a homeomorphism, for every $\mathcal T$: $h_W$ is a universal homeomorphism in the sense of [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism]. No non-flat section-base-change isomorphism is asserted: the tensor extension here is the base change of the already constructed affine space $H_W$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.9(3), last two sentences of proof; Lemma 5.2.6, Definition 3.3.1, Proposition 3.3.5; Stacks 0BR8, 081V, 0DTQ; primary published PDF read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The family $(W\to T)$ is jointly surjective and etale, and step 7 proves that every $h_W:H_W\to W$ is a universal homeomorphism. By [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism], $h$ is a universal homeomorphism. Its base change by every algebraic-space morphism $T'\to T$ therefore induces the required homeomorphism of point spaces. Together with steps 1, 4 and 5, this proves every clause of the item. The construction used only arbitrary-base-change stability of qcqs, adequate affineness over affine targets, and tensor extensions in the algebra-unit lemma; there was no flatness, finite-type, Noetherian or absolute diagonal-separation restriction.
